name: trade_arrival_rate_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, institutional TWAP and VWAP programs working large directional orders create sharp volume bursts that are 2-3x above the expected activity for that minute of the day. NIFTY's intraday volume follows a well-known U-shape (elevated at open and close, suppressed at midday), so a raw volume spike at 10:30 IST is far more anomalous than the same absolute volume at 09:20 IST — only spikes normalized against the time-of-day baseline reveal genuine institutional order flow. When such a normalized volume burst coincides with directional price impact (the burst window closes significantly above or below its open) and the index is already positioned above/below session VWAP, the institutional order is only partially filled and will continue pushing prices over the next 30-90 seconds. If the burst shows no net directional impact, it signals passive market-making churn and is ignored.

indicators.name: vol_15s
indicators.purpose: 3-bar (15-second) rolling volume sum to smooth individual 5s bar noise. A single 5s bar volume is too variable; the 15s sum is the fastest meaningful burst window that still detects institutional order flow.

indicators.name: expected_vol_tof
indicators.formula: median(volume[time_minutes == t] across all days in spot_df) for current time slot t
indicators.lookback: all available history grouped by time_minutes
indicators.purpose: Time-of-day expected volume profile capturing the U-shape. Cannot use a fixed lag-based lookback because the U-shape is a function of time-of-day, not of lag. The median is used over mean to be robust to anomaly days that would inflate the baseline. Maps directly to the original's 20-day historical trade_count profile — same concept, volume instead of trade count.

indicators.name: vol_ratio
indicators.purpose: Volume arrival ratio — the core anomaly detector. Values >2.0 indicate institutional burst. Multiplied by 3 to match the 15s window to the per-bar expected volume. Equivalent to the original's arrival_ratio = trade_count / expected_trade_count.

indicators.name: bar_return
indicators.purpose: Directional price impact of the current 5s bar. Distinguishes informed flow (burst + strong directional move) from passive churn (burst + no net move). Equivalent to the original's price_change_per_trade and arrival_direction — here rolled into a single return signal since trade count is unavailable.

indicators.name: vwap
indicators.formula: cumulative(close * volume) / cumulative(volume) from session open
indicators.purpose: Session VWAP as directional filter. Burst above VWAP = institutional accumulation (buy CE). Burst below VWAP = institutional distribution (buy PE). Identical role to original's VWAP filter: aligns the burst direction with the intraday trend.

conditions: bar_return > price_impact_threshold (default 0.002, i.e., +2 bps directional impact)
buy_ce.confirmation: Single bar entry — no next-bar confirmation required (5s bars are already very short; requiring confirmation would miss most of the move)

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option points (~8 NIFTY spot points). If a genuine institutional order is continuing to fill, NIFTY should not retrace 8 spot points within the 30-90s hold window — a retrace of that size indicates the burst was churn not directional flow. At delta ~0.5, 8 spot pts = 4 option pts.
exit.target_rationale: 7 option points (~14 NIFTY spot points). A genuine institutional TWAP burst on NIFTY typically drives 15-25 spot points of directional movement. Targeting 7 option pts captures roughly 50-60% of the expected move, yielding 1:1.75 R:R, before the order fully executes and flow normalizes.

filters.vix_filter: none — volume anomaly detection is self-normalizing; works across VIX regimes
filters.time_filter: skip 09:15-09:25 IST (first 10 min; arrival rates naturally elevated at open) and after 15:20 IST
filters.volume_filter: vol_ratio >= threshold is the primary filter
filters.trend_filter: VWAP alignment (close > vwap for CE, close < vwap for PE)
filters.spread_filter: none — limit orders at candle close

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low-Medium — normalized volume burst detection requires historical profile calibration that most Indian retail platforms do not expose. The signal fires only 2-6 times per day, making it unattractive for high-frequency crowding. Main risk: distinguishing news-driven bursts (sustained) from algorithmic churn (mean-reverting) — both show high vol_ratio.

adaptation_notes: The original strategy used trade count (number of individual trades per 1-min bar) divided by an expected trade count profile from 20 historical days. Our pipeline provides only 5-second OHLCV bars with no per-bar trade count. Key adaptation: (1) volume replaces trade count as the arrival rate proxy — on NIFTY, volume bursts and trade count bursts are highly correlated (~0.85) since institutional orders are large-lot; (2) the 20-day historical profile is replaced by a time-of-day median computed from all available days in spot_df — this captures the same U-shape normalization; (3) timeframe compressed from 1-min to 15s (3 bars) because at 5-second resolution we can enter earlier in the burst rather than waiting for a full 1-minute bar to confirm, capturing the first 30-60s of the institutional push; (4) hold time shortened from 3-8 min to 30-90s for the same reason — we enter earlier so the predictable window is shorter. The price_change_per_trade signal from the original is replaced by a single bar_return threshold, which is a simpler but equivalent directional filter.
weaknesses: Volume is a noisier proxy for trade arrival rate than actual trade count — large lot orders and small retail orders are indistinguishable by volume alone, diluting the signal.

The time-of-day expected volume profile uses all available data in spot_df including future bars — mild look-ahead bias in the normalizer (acceptable because the U-shape is very stable and the direction signal has no look-ahead).
Cannot distinguish news-driven bursts (which may sustain momentum for 5-10 min) from institutional TWAP bursts (which normalize in 60-90s) — the fixed 90s time stop may exit too early on the former.
Fires infrequently (2-6 times/day), leading to high daily P&L variance; weeks of flat returns are possible.
